design_rationale:
WHY A GOOD TEST: a Texas SR-22 non-owner insured whose requirement ended asks to finish her signed cancellation and learn the refund (her own tool). The return depends on a premium-written entry the late-renewal workflow never booked: the agent must see the renewal term carries only its fee, start from the renewal offer premium recorded on the term and carry only what changed since the offer was issued (the SR-22 moved to Cardinal Point afterwards, the renewal plan, the lapse), pick the charging basis from the filing record, book it, and only then figure the return with its short-rate table, term-origin and run-off rules.
SCOPE: task 0 claims nonowner_ext_late_renewal_written (state_due, agent) and nonowner_ext_insured_cancel_return (on_request, user).
DRAW: prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5,4]; return 5, late-renewal written premium 4 (the draw lets the author assign the counts; round 7 moved the 5 to the return when P1's returned-payment change was struck as not exactly computable).
PROBLEM TREE: root nonowner_ext_insured_cancel_return <- nonowner_ext_late_renewal_written (value_input, state form: 'The requested-cancellation return is fixed only after the term's premium ledger carries a premium-written entry for the term.'); only the late-renewal booking tool writes a premium-written entry. Opening falsity: net written 0.00, fee-only ledger. Skip run: 0.00 vs 1205.23.
FACTOR CARD late-renewal (expected 1449.71, whole baseline 1244.32): late_filer_change -> 1260.62; late_lapse_relativity -> 1367.65; late_plan_change -> 1542.24; late_charging_basis -> 1425.81. Standard figure: the recorded full-term premium 1265.17 (the offer, which carried the June return and no requirement). XF26: every factor carries a change since the 2026-09-10 issue date or the transaction's own method; reading the recorded premium and applying lapse and plan alone gives 1260.62, not the gold. Method: flat full-term charge (certified on every lapse day) vs certified-days share vs per-day share. Near-misses: withdrawn SR-22 duplicate; stale certificate field none; both returned payments (no rule re-rates payment history after the offer); an exclusive lapse count of 2 days would fall to the no-relativity tier.
FACTOR CARD return (expected 1205.23, whole baseline 1254.56): requirement_relief -> 1120.07; elapsed_term_scale -> 1233.62; term_origin_scale -> 1212.98; plan_retention_scale -> 1183.94; certificate_runoff -> 1301.95. Multi-source: requirement_relief (request reason x filing), late filer change (filing status and dates x term dates and points), late charging basis (filing date x lapse dates). Cross-difficulty: fr, billing.
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: premium written - nonowner_premium_charging.term_status (in_force). Return - nonowner_insured_cancellation.signed_request, no_backdating, nonowner_unearned_premium_return.term_status. Overwrites: premium_charging premium-written sentence (late renewals only); insured_cancellation and unearned_premium_return retention and transaction-by-transaction sentences (other cancellations restated in full).
SEED: TX profile; term 1 expired (1216.51), term 2 in force with lapse (offer 1265.17); plan 1 Six-Pay fully paid (20% down + fee, five installments, June check returned with NSF fee, one late fee, installment 5 bank payment returned 2026-09-14 and repaid 2026-09-15 by debit card with the NSF fee and the SR-22 filing fee charged that day; certified funds on every open plan from 2026-09-14 after the second return in twelve months); plan 2 Paid-in-Full (renewal bill paid 2026-10-12 by debit card, credit balance until the premium posts); fr SR-22 Operator carrier transfer requested 2026-09-15 (after the offer; she came off her mother's car policy, whose carrier sends its own SR-26), filed 2026-09-16, and a withdrawn duplicate.
PERSONA: brisk home health aide; volunteers only the goal; credentials, form details, renewal timing, payment history and the September filing transfer only when asked; agrees to preliminary work after the agent explains it; runs the hand-over tool once; closes on the cancellation and the return figure.
STANDARD SOLUTION: verify -> reads -> book premium written 1449.71 (182 days from 2026-10-10) -> hand over the cancellation with return 1205.23, 162 days, effective 2026-10-17.
VERIFICATION: scratch harness (check_compute.build_env + real tool bodies on a dict world), per-factor baseline substitution and the skip run; figures above are its output.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Vance, thirty-five, a home health aide in Houston who drives clients' cars and rentals but owns no car of her own. You speak politely and a little briskly, between appointments, and you like plain answers. Texas made you carry an SR-22 after an old ticket-and-insurance problem; your previous insurer had been filing it on your mother's car policy, where you were listed as a driver, and in September, when she took you off that policy, you had Cardinal Point take the filing over, and the state's letter said the requirement ran through October 16, 2026. You kept your Cardinal Point non-owner policy going until then, and you mailed in the signed cancellation form asking for the policy to be cancelled as of October 17, 2026, because the requirement ended. You are calling to get that cancellation finished today and to find out how much premium you will get back. You are fine with the representative looking into your account and doing whatever they need to do on their side for this, and you will do anything they say you have to do yourself. You open by saying who you are and that you want to finish cancelling your non-owner policy now that your SR-22 period is over, and know what you will be getting back. When the representative asks for details to find and verify you, you give your phone number, 7135555184, and your date of birth, 1991-03-22; if they ask for more, the last four of your driver's license are 5629 and your ZIP code is 77023. If they ask about the form, you say you mailed it in and it was dated for the cancellation to start October 17, 2026, and that the reason was that the state requirement ended. If they ask about your renewal, you remember the policy ran out on October 10 and you paid the renewal online on October 12, a couple of days late. If they ask about payments, you say a check bounced in June and the online bank payment for your last installment bounced in September, and you paid that one by debit card the next day. If they ask whether you have any other insurance, own a car or plan to buy one, you say no. You do not know anything about how premiums or refunds are worked out and you never suggest a figure; if a number is read to you, you just listen. If the representative explains that something has to be taken care of on the account first, you say that is fine and to go ahead. When the representative tells you the cancellation is something you put through yourself and gives you the tool with the details to enter, you run it once with exactly the values they give you and read back what it shows. Once you have been told the policy is cancelled and how much premium is being returned, you thank them and end the call without asking for anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.written_amount: 1449.71 = RND(late-renewal rated premium 1449.7077 x charging share 1): recorded full-term premium 1265.17 (the 2026-09-10 offer) x filer change 1.15 (the SR-22 requirement was requested 2026-09-15, after the issue date, with 8 points; nothing released) x lapse 1.06 (3 days both included) x plan change 0.94/1.00 (renewal Paid-in-Full plan over the expiring term's Six-Pay plan); charging share 1 because the SR-22 Operator certificate was filed 2026-09-16, before the first lapse day, and its certified-through date 2026-10-16 (its required-through date, no certificate end date being recorded) is on or after the last lapse day 2026-10-12 ('the company stayed certified on every lapse day, the charging share is one, a flat full-term charge').
argument_uniqueness_tracing.nonowner_policy_id: Value: renewal term 2. Basis: the in-force term with the recorded lapse; docstring 'the Named Non-Owner Policy renewal term the premium is written on'. Uniqueness: term 1 is expired with its premium written.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.effective_date: Value: 2026-10-10. Basis: the flat charge is 'booked from the renewal term's effective date with the renewal term's days as its days'. Uniqueness: the in-force date 2026-10-13 belongs to the per-day bases only.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.premium_days: Value: 182. Basis: the renewal term's days (2026-10-10 to 2027-04-10). Uniqueness: 179 days in force belongs to the per-day bases only.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.return_amount: 1205.23 = RND(unearned premium 1290.4012 x (1 - 6.60/100)). Unearned = written 1449.71 x 162 / 182; unearned days = 175 standard (2026-10-17 to 2027-04-10) less 3 SR-26 transmission and 10 run-off days of the filed SR-22 Operator certificate. Retention 10.0 x 0.5 (requirement ended, required-through 2026-10-16 on or before 2026-10-17) x 1.5 (7/182 of the term run) x 1.10 (renewal term with a lapse recorded) x 0.80 (Paid-in-Full plan) = 6.60 percent.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.nonowner_policy_id: Value: renewal term 2. Basis: the request row names this term; it is the only in_force term. Uniqueness: term 1 is expired.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.nonowner_cancel_request_id: Value: the request reference read from find_nonowner_cancellation_requests. Basis: the docstring asks for 'the named insured's signed cancellation request for that term'. Uniqueness: it is the only request on file.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.cancellation_effective_date: Value: 2026-10-17. Basis: 'the cancellation effective date is the requested date on the signed request when that is on or after the date the request was received' (requested 2026-10-17, received 2026-10-14). Uniqueness: the received date applies only to an earlier requested date.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.premium_days: Value: 162. Basis: 'with the unearned days used as its days'; 175 - 13 after the run-off method. Uniqueness: 175 is the standard count.

edges.condition: nonowner_premium_transactions holds a row with event_type nonowner_premium_written for the term
edges.policy_source: The requested-cancellation return is fixed only after the term's premium ledger carries a premium-written entry for the term.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The renewal term's only premium-ledger entry is the renewal policy fee and its net written premium is 0.00, so no premium-written entry exists for the term.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The booking at step 12 creates the premium-written entry (1449.71 USD, 182 days) and sets term_written_premium to 1449.71; written_premium_on_term then reads 1449.71 instead of 0.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite edge: the premium-written entry must stand before the return is figured, as the prerequisite sentence states; there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the premium booking leaves written_premium_on_term 0, so the return recomputes to 0.00 instead of 1205.23, and the terminal ledger lacks the 1449.71 entry.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to finish the cancellation and learn the refund; it never mentions premium being written, the renewal premium, a missing entry or anything to be sorted out first. Her renewal-payment memory is given only when asked, and she agrees to preliminary work only after the agent says it is needed.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: cancel_nonowner_term_6aabad38 updates the term and creates the return entry with whatever amount it is given and never reads the premium ledger; book_renewal_written_premium_ed68a083 creates the entry without checking status or lapse. Neither raises or hints on an unmet prerequisite (task_tools.py function bodies).
